preconditions.description: The number of vertices n is an integer between 1 and 2¹⁶ (inclusive).

preconditions.expression: all(0 <= degree_v <= n - 1 for degree_v, _ in degrees_and_sums)
preconditions.description: For each vertex v, degree_v is an integer between 0 and n-1 (inclusive), representing the number of adjacent vertices.

preconditions.expression: all(0 <= s_v < 2**16 for _, s_v in degrees_and_sums)
preconditions.description: For each vertex v, s_v is an integer between 0 and 2¹⁶-1 (inclusive), representing the XOR sum of degrees of adjacent vertices.

preconditions.expression: sum(degree_v for degree_v, _ in degrees_and_sums) == 2 * m
preconditions.description: The sum of all degrees is even (since it equals twice the number of edges m in the forest).

preconditions.expression: degrees_and_sums == [(degree_v, s_v) for degree_v, s_v in zip(degrees, sums)]
preconditions.description: degrees_and_sums is a list of tuples (degree_v, s_v) for each vertex v, where degrees and sums are parsed from stdin.

postconditions.expression: m == sum(degree_v // 2 for degree_v, _ in degrees_and_sums)
postconditions.description: m is the number of edges in the forest, computed as half the sum of all degrees (since each edge contributes to two degrees).

postconditions.expression: all(0 <= a < n and 0 <= b < n and a != b for a, b in edges)
postconditions.description: Each edge (a, b) consists of two distinct vertices a and b, both in the range [0, n-1].
The number of edges printed equals m.

postconditions.expression: all(degree_v == len([b for a, b in edges if a == v or b == v]) for v, (degree_v, _) in enumerate(degrees_and_sums))
postconditions.description: For each vertex v, its degree in the output graph matches the given degree_v.

postconditions.expression: all(s_v == (sum(degree_u for u in neighbors if u != v) ^ degree_v) for v, (degree_v, s_v) in enumerate(degrees_and_sums) if degree_v > 0)
postconditions.description: For each vertex v with degree_v > 0, the XOR sum of degrees of its neighbors equals s_v. Here, neighbors are vertices connected to v in the output graph.

postconditions.expression: not any(a == b for a, b in edges)
postconditions.description: No edge connects a vertex to itself (no loops).

postconditions.expression: not any((a1 == b2 and a2 == b1) for (a1, b1) in edges for (a2, b2) in edges if (a1, b1) != (a2, b2))
postconditions.description: No two edges are parallel (no duplicate edges).
The output graph is acyclic (no directed cycles when treated as undirected). The helper is_acyclic(edges, n) checks for cycles using a union-find or DFS/BFS approach.
